पिंस् पिंस्, cl. 1. 10. P. पिंसति, पिं-
सितुम्, पिंसयति, -यितुम्, to speak; to
shine.
पिनस पिनस, अस्, m. = पीनस, q. v.

पीनस पीनस, अस्, m. (probably अपि + नस्
= नासा; by some connected with पीन), cough,
catarrh; cold affecting the nose, inflammation of the
schneiderian membrane [cf. अपी-नस]; (आ), f. the
plant Cucumis Utilissimus (= कर्कटी).
पिनह् पि-नह् = अपि-नह्, q. v.

पि-नद्ध, अस्, आ, अम्, tied on, put on, fastened,
bound; dressed, accoutred; wrapped, covered, con-
cealed; pierced, penetrated.

पिनद्धक, अस्, इका, अम्, dressed, clothed,
covered.
पि-नह्य, ind. having put on or dressed.

पिनाक पिनाक, अस्, अम्, m. n. (said to be
fr. rt. 3. पा), a staff, stick; a bow; the club or bow
of Rudra-Śiva; a trident or three-pronged spear;
the trident of Śiva; a shower or fall of dust, falling
dust; (अस्), m., N. of a man; (ई), f. a kind of
stringed instrument, a sort of violin.
—पिनाक-
गोप्तृ, ता, m. ‘preserver of the Pināka,’ an epithet
of Śiva.
—पिनाक-धृक् (see धृक्), or पिनाक-
भृत्, त्, m. ‘bearer of the Pināka,’ an epithet of
Śiva.
—पिनाक-पाणि, इस्, m. ‘Pināka in hand,’ an
epithet of Śiva.

पिनाकि, इस्, इस्, इ (occurring only in acc. sing.),
substituted for पिनाकिन्, q. v.

पिनाकिन्, ई, इनी, इ, armed with a Pināka; (ई), m.
an epithet of Rudra-Śiva; N. of one of the eleven
Rudras; (इनी), f., N. of two rivers.
—पिनाकिनी-
माहात्म्य, अम्, n., N. of a part of the Brahmāṇḍa-
Purāṇa.

पिन्यास पिन्यास, अम्, n. (said to be fr. rt.
2. अस् with पि-नि), Asa Fœtida; [cf. पिण्याक.]

पिन्व् पिन्व्, cl. 1. P. A. पिन्वति, -ते,
पिपिन्व, पिपिन्वे, पिन्विष्यति, -ते,
पिन्वितुम्, Ved. to cause to swell, to distend, to cause
to overflow or run over, to cause to abound; to cause
to abound in milk (Ṛg-veda

, where,
according to Sāy., पिन्वथः = पयसा पूरित-
वन्तौ); to sprinkle, wet, moisten, water; to dis-
charge, pour forth; to grant, bestow; (A.) to swell,
to be distended, to overflow; [cf. rt. प्यै.]

पिन्व, अस्, आ, अम्, Ved. causing to swell or flow;
[cf. दानु-प्˚.]

पिन्वन, अम्, n., Ved. a particular vessel used in
religious ceremonies.

पिन्वन्त्यपीया, f., Ved., scil. ऋच्, an epithet of
the verse beginning पिन्वन्त्य् अपो (Ṛg-veda

पिन्वमान, अस्, आ, अम्, Ved. being swollen,
swelling, being full or filled.

पीन पीन, अस्, आ, अम् (fr. rt. प्यै), fat,
fleshy, brawny, muscular; swelling, swollen, large,
corpulent, thick, plump; full, round; profuse (e. g.
पीनः स्वेदः, profuse perspiration); [cf. पीवर;
Gr. πῑαρός, πῖας, πΐων, πιμελή; Lat. pinguis;
Iceland. feit-r, ‘fat;’ Angl. Sax. fœtt; Old Germ.
feizt = Mod. Germ. feist, fett.]
—पीन-तरल, अस्,
आ, अम्, having a large central gem.
—पीन-ता, f.
fatness, corpulency (opposed to कृश-ता).
—पीन-
नितम्बा, f. ‘having full hips,’ N. of a metre, four
times ¯¯¯¯ , ¯˘˘¯¯ , ¯¯¯˘˘¯¯ .
—पीन-वक्-
षस्, आस्, आस्, अस्, large-chested, full-breasted, having
a large or full breast.
—पीन-श्रोणीपयोधरा, f.
having swelling hips and breasts.
—पीनोत्तुङ्ग-
स्तनी (˚न-उत्˚), f. (a woman) having a large and
prominent breast.
—पीनोध्नी (˚न-ऊध्˚), f. a cow
with full or swelling udders (also पीनोधस्, आस्, f.;
cf. ऊधस्, घटोध्नी).
पीनसिन्, ई, इनी, इ, having a cold.
